sections.h2: What is the way to contact Tyrrell County's deed office?
sections.html:
Find the office at 403 Main Street in Columbia, NC 27925, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 449. The listed phone is (252) 796-2901 and the fax line is (252) 796-0148.

Office hours on the register's own site are 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, with holidays excluded. Plan any visit so that it falls inside those hours. If you are mailing a deed, use the post office box and call first so the office can tell you what else it needs.

Tyrrell County is the least populated of the four counties in a Census comparison used here, with 3,537 residents in mid-2025 across 390.78 square miles of land. That works out to 8.3 people per square mile.

According to the register's site, the office lets a property owner put the world on notice of an ownership interest. That public record shields later parties from unknown transactions and hidden liens.

The filing cabinet there ranges from old land grants to modern deeds, maps, leases and agreements. The same counter hands out vital certificates and marriage licenses.

A Fraud Alert Notification Service is advertised on the site. Registering an email address brings an automatic message whenever a recording looks possibly fraudulent. Owners of vacant land or of property they do not live at may find the alert useful, since they are not at the parcel to notice anything.

sections.h2: Who settles the conveyance tax on a Tyrrell County deed?
sections.html:
The seller does. The statute names the person transferring title as the one who settles the tax at the register's office, ahead of recording.

The excise tax statute sets a flat charge per $500 block of price or value, with leftovers counted as a full block. The county and the State share what comes in.

Do not estimate the dollar figure yourself. The attorney or title agent running your closing can read it off the settlement statement, and the Columbia counter can help if you are filing alone.

sections.h2: What other costs come with recording in Tyrrell County?
sections.html:
Recording charges are statewide, so Tyrrell County charges what the General Statutes set. Everything below comes straight from the statute pages, and you should confirm any special items with the Columbia office before you send a package.

Statutory charges that can apply to a Tyrrell County recording
ItemFee as printedSource
Basic instrument, first 15 pages$26.00G.S. 161-10
Each added page$4.00G.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each afterG.S. 161-10
Release of a mortgage lienFree of chargeG.S. 161-10
Deed excise taxPer $500 block of valueG.S. 105-228.30

The statute treats the list as complete, and payment is due when the document is presented.

sections.h2: What do Tyrrell County's Census figures show?
sections.html:
The 2020-2024 QuickFacts median for an owned home is $164,500, and 77.8% of homes are owner-lived. Rent in the middle runs $644 a month, and household income in the middle is $41,685.

Housing units totaled 2,052 in July 2025, and builders took out 18 permits in 2025. The 1,547 households average 1.94 people, and 23.3% of residents have passed 65. Workers face a 34.2 minute average commute, the longest among the four counties compared.

  • Population was 4,407 in the 2010 Census and 3,245 in 2020.
  • The July 2025 estimate of 3,537 is 9.0% above the April 2020 estimate base.
  • Persons in poverty stand at 19.5%.

In a county of fewer than 3,600 residents, if the property came to you from a relative, ask a title company to review the chain of title before you list it or accept an offer, and keep any estate paperwork together with the deed.

Persons without health insurance under age 65 are 13.8% in the same table, and 83.5% of people in that age bracket finished high school. The county also shows 71 employer establishments and 543 employees in 2023.

sections.h2: What does the Tyrrell County population look like?
sections.html:
Knowing the neighbors helps a seller judge how a listing will be read. QuickFacts breaks the county down as 63.6% White alone, 28.6% Black alone, 13.1% Hispanic or Latino of any race, and 1.6% American Indian and Alaska Native alone. Veterans number 248 for 2020-2024.

  • Residents living at their prior-year address: 88.9%.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 80.9%, which affects buyers who work remotely.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 71, with 543 employees.
  • Retail sales in 2022: $53,963 thousand, or $15,538 per person.

Owners who inherit land here sometimes live far away. If that describes you, the register's fraud alert, a clear title review and a local contact for the closer all make a long-distance sale easier. Children under 18 are 18.5% of the population, foreign-born residents are 5.7%, and 13.0% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or more. Households with a computer are 82.4% of the total, so paper mail and phone calls remain useful alongside any e-recording.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter after I sell a Tyrrell County house?
sections.html:
G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from an unregistered deed against creditors and later buyers who gave value. The deed that reaches the county office first usually ranks ahead.

If your deed is not recorded, a creditor with a claim against you, or a second buyer, could end up ahead of the purchaser. The practical answer is to make sure the deed is on its way to Columbia on closing day, whether through your closer or by your own delivery.

  • Ask when the recording will happen and how it will be submitted.
  • Keep proof of delivery if you mail the deed to P.O. Box 449.
  • Request the recording information once the register has filed it.

sections.h2: How are Tyrrell County property taxes paid and handled at a sale?
sections.html:
Interest rules sit in G.S. 105-360, and G.S. 105-355 explains the lien that follows the parcel.

Tyrrell County's payment page offers six routes: web portal, phone, mail, the tax office counter, a drop box inside the hallway before the tax department door, and a bank's bill pay. It says card payments carry either a $2.50 or a 2.95% service fee, whichever is greater, and e-check payments an added $2.00 fee. A bank's bill pay can lag by as much as seven business days, so begin early.

For the current bill, tax rate and any prepayment discount, ask the Tyrrell County tax office.

sections.h2: Can an heir sell a Tyrrell County house without a full estate?
sections.html:
Sometimes. G.S. 28A-25-1 allows an affidavit for small estates, with caps of $20,000 in personal property after liens and $30,000 for a sole-heir surviving spouse after any spousal allowance, if no personal representative petition is pending and 30 days have passed since death.

File it with the superior court clerk where the person lived. The statute has the affidavit describe every tract of land the person owned. Whether you can then deed the land is a question for an attorney. Ask the clerk of court about the forms, and ask the register what must be recorded to show the heirs' authority to convey.

faqs.q: What are the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Nine to five on weekdays that are not holidays, the site says. Find it at 403 Main Street in Columbia or call (252) 796-2901.

faqs.q: Is there a fraud alert for Tyrrell County property records?
faqs.a: Yes. The register offers a Fraud Alert Notification Service that emails you if a possibly fraudulent recording is made. Sign up through the register's website.

faqs.q: Who owes the conveyance tax in Tyrrell County?
faqs.a: The seller, before recording.  Look for the figure on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: What does a basic recording cost in Tyrrell County?
faqs.a: The base charge covers the first 15 pages, with a per-page charge after that, as the fee statute lays out. Ask the office whether your document triggers extra charges.

faqs.q: Does the Tyrrell County register collect property taxes?
faqs.a: No. The tax office takes property tax payments, and the county's payment page lists the ways to pay. Ask that office for your bill before closing.
